items.followUp: Define a coordinate covalent bond and state how it differs from an ordinary covalent bond.

rubric.why: Mutual sharing of electron pairs is the defining feature of a covalent bond.
rubric.description: Defines a covalent bond as one formed by mutual sharing of electron pair(s) between atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atoms mutually share electron pair(s).

rubric.why: The question also asks for the three types of covalent bond.
rubric.description: Names single, double and triple covalent bonds.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming all three types.

modelAnswer: A covalent bond is formed when two atoms mutually share one or more pairs of electrons.
Its three types are single, double and triple covalent bonds.

items.followUp: How do stronger intermolecular forces affect the boiling point of a liquid?

rubric.why: The strength of intermolecular forces affects the rate of evaporation.
rubric.description: States that stronger intermolecular forces slow evaporation, while weaker forces allow faster evaporation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating either relationship.

rubric.why: Evaporation occurs when molecules escape from the liquid surface; stronger attractions make escape more difficult.
rubric.description: Explains the effect of intermolecular forces in terms of molecules escaping from the liquid.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking stronger forces with fewer molecules escaping, or weaker forces with easier escape.

modelAnswer: Stronger intermolecular forces hold liquid molecules more tightly, so fewer molecules can escape from the surface and evaporation is slower.
Weaker intermolecular forces allow molecules to escape more easily, so evaporation is faster.

items.followUp: What happens to the forward and reverse reaction rates when a reversible reaction reaches dynamic equilibrium?

rubric.why: Equal forward and reverse reaction rates are essential to dynamic equilibrium.
rubric.description: States that the forward and reverse reaction rates are equal.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explicitly stating that the two rates are equal.

rubric.why: At equilibrium, equal rates mean there is no net change in the concentrations of reactants and products.
rubric.description: States that reactant and product concentrations remain constant.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that concentrations remain constant at equilibrium.

modelAnswer: Dynamic equilibrium is the state in a closed system where the forward and reverse reactions continue at equal rates.
The concentrations of reactants and products remain constant.

items.followUp: What is meant by the scattering of light by a colloid?

rubric.why: The Tyndall effect is caused by colloidal particles scattering light.
rubric.description: Identifies scattering of light by colloidal particles as the cause of the Tyndall effect.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying colloidal particles as the cause of light scattering.

rubric.why: Scattering makes the path of a light beam visible through a colloid.
rubric.description: States that the scattered beam or its path becomes visible.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the path of the beam becomes visible.

modelAnswer: Colloidal particles scatter a beam of light passing through a colloid.
This scattering makes the path of the beam visible; this phenomenon is called the Tyndall effect.
